Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our bottom-up cost model puts the full cost of this part at EUR 24.31 per unit (cost:340010).
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 10.1% (fc:340010@2026-09).
Our last 3 orders for this part were at EUR 29.89 per unit (po:4500014436-10, po:4500014383-10, po:4500014337-10).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

decisions.tactician: o4 and o3 give our lowest C (€1,416,340), lower than E0's €1,449,940, because the 42 d lead time is a must-have for us. o4's 36-month commitment speaks most directly to its strong planning_security need, and the 'to it' figure does not count contract length. That partly offsets the 56 d lead E0 offered it, so o4 has a better chance of acceptance than o3 at the same C. At €29.95 the price sits well below its quote but above its health price, so it is a firm and credible opening. o5/o6 risk refusal because it cannot deliver faster under full capacity, and o7 costs far more.

decisions.tactician: o4 keeps the 36-month binding term the supplier values for planning security, and the 42 d lead time. It gives our lowest C of €1,440,838, better than E0's €1,474,438 on the 56 d lead and equal to o3/o5/o6. The 36-month term is a concession the supplier already accepted and values, so it is likely to draw a better counter than the 24-month variants. The delivery record argument (a1) is a new kind and undercuts the lead-time premium. Accepting now at €31.70 or €33.60 would leave value on the table while it is still moving.
